spec.functions: dav1d_wiener_filter7_8bpc_rvv (c->wiener[0], 7-tap) and dav1d_wiener_filter5_8bpc_rvv (c->wiener[1], 5-tap: filter[k][0] = filter[k][6] = 0), both with the signature of decl_lr_filter_fn at BITDEPTH 8: (pixel *dst, ptrdiff_t stride, const pixel (*left)[4], const pixel *lpf, int w, int h, const LooprestorationParams *params, enum LrEdgeFlags edges)
spec.formula: wiener_c in context/reference_looprestoration_tmpl.c at 8bpc. Horizontal pass per row (wiener_filter_h): sum = (1 << 14) + 128*src[x] + sum_i fh[i]*t(x+i-3), out = iclip((sum + 4) >> 3, 0, 8191) (u16 intermediate); edge pixels t(j) come from left[][], src[-3..-1] or src[0] (LR_HAVE_LEFT) and src[w..w+2] or src[w-1] (LR_HAVE_RIGHT). Vertical pass (wiener_filter_v/hv): sum = -(1 << 18) + sum_k fv[k]*row_k[x], out = iclip_pixel((sum + 1024) >> 11). Rows above/below come from lpf (2 rows at lpf, 2 rows at lpf + 6*stride) when LR_HAVE_TOP/BOTTOM, else the edge row is repeated
spec.domain: 1 <= w <= 384 (w == 256 when LR_HAVE_RIGHT), 1 <= h <= 64; taps symmetric (filter[k][i] == filter[k][6-i], as the decoder and checkasm build them); f0 in [-5,10], f1 in [-23,8], f2 in [-17,46], filter[0][3] = -2*(f0+f1+f2), filter[1][3] = 128 - 2*(f0+f1+f2); pixels 0..255
width_bounds: horizontal intermediate: 128*255 + taps*255 + 2^14 fits in 17 bits signed before the shift; after >> 3 and the clip it is 13 bits (0..8191)
vertical: sum of 7 products of 13-bit values and 8-bit taps needs 32 bits before >> 11
writes past w in a dst row are allowed up to w rounded up to 64 pixels (checkasm_check_pixel_padded_align(..., 64, 1)); nothing else outside the w x h block may change
every VLEN from 128 to 1024; plain RVV 1.0 plus Zba/Zbb (the X280 has no Zbs, no Zvbb)

regimes.bench: checkasm --bench: w=256, h=64, all four edges (LR_HAVE_LEFT|RIGHT|TOP|BOTTOM), one cell per function: wiener_7tap_8bpc and wiener_5tap_8bpc
regimes.check: checkasm: random w in 1..384, h in 1..64, every one of the 16 edge combinations, random taps in the domain, and the padded-align output check

candidates.application: one vsetvl-driven loop over the row width per pass; the tail is a smaller vl, no scalar epilogue
candidates.expected_gain: removes scalar tail code; the baseline structure of any RVV port
preconditions: the padded-align rule allows writing up to align(w, 64)

candidates.title: Add mirrored pixel pairs before multiplying (symmetric taps)
candidates.application: filter[i] == filter[6-i]: add t(x-3)+t(x+3), t(x-2)+t(x+2), t(x-1)+t(x+1) first, then 3 multiplies plus the centre instead of 7 (4-tap form for the 5-tap filter); the vertical pass pairs rows the same way
candidates.expected_gain: about 40% fewer multiplies in both passes
preconditions: symmetric taps are part of the domain (decoder and checkasm)
pair sums of u8 fit in 9 bits, of 13-bit intermediates in 14 bits

candidates.application: do the horizontal pass in 16-bit lanes: |sum| stays below 2^15 for the domain's taps once the 2^14 offset is folded in (arm64 computes it in int16 with a saturating add and stores the result biased by -2048, compensated in the vertical pass)
candidates.expected_gain: twice the lanes per register for the horizontal pass
preconditions: prove the int16 range per tap envelope or use a saturating add whose clamp matches iclip

candidates.application: vwmulu/vwmaccsu/vwmacc from u8 pixels and s16 taps (horizontal) or u16 rows and taps (vertical) instead of extend then multiply
preconditions: signedness of each operand matches the instruction (vwmaccsu: signed scalar, unsigned vector)

candidates.application: vmacc/vwmacc chains for the tap sums
taps as scalar operands (.vx) loaded once per call

candidates.title: One pass per output row over a ring of filtered rows
candidates.application: keep the last 6 horizontally filtered rows in a stack ring buffer (384 u16 each) and, per new row, run the horizontal pass and immediately the vertical pass for one output row (arm64 wiener_filter7_hv); rotate pointers, never copy rows
candidates.expected_gain: each source row is filtered horizontally once and the vertical pass reads rows still in L1
preconditions: stack frame within the psABI (16-byte aligned, restored)
top/bottom edge handling with lpf rows as in wiener_c

candidates.title: Build the shifted pixel vectors with slides from one load
candidates.application: load vl+6 pixels once and derive the 7 tap vectors with vslidedown (or keep overlapping unit-stride vle8 loads at offsets 0..6: unaligned byte loads are cheap); measure both on the X280
candidates.expected_gain: fewer loads per output, or fewer permutes: depends on the X280's load vs slide cost
preconditions: slides read past vl only inside the loaded group

candidates.title: Handle the left/right padding outside the main loop
candidates.application: materialize the padded row (3 pixels each side from left[], src[-3..], or replicated edge pixels) only for the first and last vector, or into a small stack row, so the main loop has no edge logic
preconditions: exactly the C's padding cases for every edge flag

candidates.application: LMUL 4-8 for the 16-bit horizontal pass and LMUL 2-4 for 32-bit vertical sums, as far as registers allow
candidates.expected_gain: fewer loop iterations and vsetvl; at VLEN 512, e16 m8 covers a 256-pixel row in one strip
preconditions: register pressure: 7 taps of inputs plus accumulators

candidates.title: A separate 5-tap path
candidates.application: wiener_filter5 skips the outer tap pair and needs a 5-row ring (arm64 has separate filter5 functions)
candidates.expected_gain: about 2/7 less work for the 5-tap cell

candidates.application: set vtype once per pass; group same-width ops
candidates.expected_gain: fewer vsetvli in the hot loop

candidates.application: two independent output vectors per iteration to hide multiply latency on the in-order X280
sources: arm64 processes 16 pixels as two 8-lane halves

candidates.application: issue the next strip's loads before the current strip's multiply chain
taps, rounding constants and edge masks loaded once per call
ta,ma everywhere results past vl are dead
candidates.expected_gain: lets the hardware skip tail work
